summary.text: 姐 is written with 女 and 且. The Han dictionary account describes it as a regional word for “mother”; later cited examples use it for an older sister, an older woman, and a young woman. How those uses are historically connected is not established here. [ref003, ref018, ref021]

formation.text: A phonosemantic compound: 女 contributes the meaning category “woman,” while 且 is identified as the sound component. The transmitted seal-script-style illustration shows both parts, but it is a modern redraw and cannot establish the character’s earlier graphic history. [ref003, ref020, ref023, ref029]

components.text: 女 is the semantic component: it supplies the woman-related category in the compound. The cited account analyzes 姐 as 女 plus 且 but does not establish an earlier form for this component in 姐. [ref003, ref020]
且 is the visible right-hand component and is identified in the traditional analysis as phonetic. Its own original referent is not established by this evidence. [ref003, ref020, ref021]

sound_limitation.text: The cited Zhengzhang reconstruction reports similar sound material for 姐 and 且, but it is a secondary compilation with multiple 且 readings; the local Baxter–Sagart data lacks a 姐 comparison. Current readings likewise do not prove the historical role. [ref015, ref016, ref025, ref026]

sound.text: A reported Old Chinese comparison places 姐 *ʔsjaːʔ alongside one 且 reading *sʰjaːʔ. The similarity is consistent with a phonetic role, but does not by itself prove the reconstruction or component identity. [ref015, ref026]
sound.system: Old Chinese, Zhengzhang Shangfang (as reported in a secondary compilation)

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings are 姐 jiě and 且 qiě; this modern pair is metadata, not evidence for the ancient sound relationship. [ref025]

history.text: The Han-dictionary tradition transmits a seal-script form and describes 姐 as 女 plus phonetic 且. The selected seal-style image is a modern digital reconstruction, not an excavated or independently dated artifact; earlier graphic development is unresolved. [ref003, ref020, ref023, ref028, ref029]

The dictionary account reports regional terms for mother, including 姐 in Shu and 社 in Huainan. Later cited Song and Yuan examples attest 姐 in sibling-age, older-woman, and young-woman contexts. The dossier does not show whether these uses developed semantically from “mother” or reflect borrowing between words, and parallel forms are disputed. [ref003, ref013, ref018, ref021, ref022]

uncertainties.text: No secure excavated early attestation or inspected early artifact form is supplied. The evidence supports the transmitted Shuowen seal-script tradition, not a complete graphic chronology or a claim of corruption. [ref028, ref029]

The earliest attestation and historical path of the common “elder sister” sense remain unresolved. The listed later uses do not establish a continuous development from the regional “mother” use, nor establish a whole-character phonetic loan. [ref018, ref019, ref021]

The historical phonetic comparison is a reported reconstruction rather than direct pronunciation evidence. The local dataset lacks a same-system 姐–且 comparison, and official per-character reading pages were inaccessible; current readings do not settle the ancient relation. [ref016, ref017, ref025, ref026, ref027]

senses.period: Han-dictionary account; exact word and graph attestation date unresolved
senses.text: The Han-dictionary entry reports that Shu speakers called a mother 姐; it reports 社 for the corresponding Huainan usage. This attests the account’s regional gloss, not the character’s first graphic appearance. [ref003, ref012, ref020]

senses.period: Attested in Song-dynasty example; earlier chronology unresolved
senses.text: A cited Song example uses 大姐 in a sibling-age context. The adjacent dictionary entry for 姊 glosses elder sister, but does not establish when 姐 acquired this sense. [ref019, ref021]
A cited Yuan example uses 姐姐 for an older woman. Its relation to the regional mother use is not established. [ref021]
A cited Yuan song uses 姐儿 for a young woman. The evidence does not establish a dated semantic path from the earlier regional mother term. [ref021]
The supplied current definition gives “elder sister, young lady.” Its compilation does not date either sense or explain how it relates to the earlier regional mother usage. [ref006, ref018, ref021]

limitations.text: The dossier gives historical attestations and modern glosses but does not establish transitions among the mother, elder-sister, older-woman, and young-woman senses. Competing regional forms and analyses do not yield a single derivational chain. [ref013, ref018, ref022]

overview.text: 姐 combines 女, which points to a woman-related meaning, with 且 as a sound component. An old dictionary records a regional meaning “mother”; later documented uses include “elder sister” and “young woman,” with no established path between them. [ref003, ref021]

components.text: 女 supplies the woman-related meaning category in this character. [ref003]
且 is the sound component in the traditional analysis. The proposed old sound match is reconstructed, not directly recorded. [ref003, ref026]

takeaway.text: The “mother” and “elder sister/young woman” uses are both documented, but their historical connection is unresolved. [ref018, ref021]

relationships.text: In the traditional analysis of 姐, 女 supplies the woman-related semantic category. [ref003, ref020]

The traditional analysis assigns 且 the sound role; reported Zhengzhang reconstructions have similar sound material, though the evidence is secondary and the component has multiple reported readings. [ref003, ref015, ref026]
